attempts.why_died: Full R(lin): CP bit-PHP proofs need one-inequality lines (triangles); a 2-equation line covers a band needing exp many triangles, and Res(2) in R(lin) has no monotone interpolation
Narrow-line route: every R(lin) refutation of bit PHP has a line of n^Omega(1) equations (Delayer + Littlewood-Offord), so the rectangle conversion costs 2^(n^Omega(1)) and gives nothing
Braun F2 route dies over Z at step 1: false sets of integer lines are not flats (sum x_j = v/2 has a degree-v indicator)
No short refutation found: val_i distinctness is cheap, but counting needs degree-l occupancy or enumerating used-value sets
Fat lines OR_t(sum_i x_i0 = t) survive every restriction; walk ignores N, so the route also bounds weak bit PHP
Width-bounded Delayer is vacuous (L-lib-102); unbounded Alon-Furedi Delayer gives only 2^Omega(l) = poly(n)
False: one injective form sum 2^k x_k refutes any unsat CNF with 2 classes per line (union of falsified sets by res with 1,-1)
False at M=1: sum over a set A at its max pins a bit of all of A, so prefix halving refutes BPHP with O(log n) classes
EGI needs Pr[sigma falsifies L] = 2^-rank (F2 only: rank-q nested sums are all false w.p. 1/2 over Z); line-determined closure gives only width (L-lib-102)

formal_statement: ∀ p : Polynomial ℕ, ∃ l : ℕ, ∀ π : List (PEqualNP.Search.QLine (Fin (2 ^ l + 1) × Fin l)), PEqualNP.Search.IsResLinQRefutation (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.BPHP (2 ^ l + 1) l) π → p.eval (2 ^ l) < PEqualNP.Search.resLinQSize π
plain_statement: For every polynomial p there is l such that every Res(lin) refutation over the integers (lines are disjunctions of integer linear equations; combination and semantic weakening; size counts coefficient bits) of the bit pigeonhole principle with 2^l+1 pigeons and 2^l holes has size above p(2^l). Open. Kills integer linear arithmetic solvers. Known for cutting planes (Beame-Whitmeyer, ICALP 2025) and for Res(lin) over F2 per an unrefereed preprint.
title: HARD LINK: bit PHP needs superpolynomial dag-like Res(lin) refutations over the integers
